dq773c.192: A few minutes from Boccheggiano, it houses the installations of the artist Paul Fuchs: very tall structures that move and emit sounds with the wind, a place particularly loved by children.
p2n2sj.50: Sound sculptures moved by the wind in the middle of the woods.
1belzhh.347: Medieval village on a cliff of magma rock at 475 meters, in the Park of the Metalliferous Hills with a view of the Amiata, a mining center of silver and copper in the Middle Ages; the territory includes the Aldobrandesco castle of Montemassi, the village of Roccatederighi among the boulders of riolite, the mining park of Ribolla and the reserve of the torrent Farma.
1v1xhxz.459: Castello degli Aldobrandeschi mentioned in 1140 (until 1188 Rocca di Fabiano), then Sienese and from 1555 Medici, seat of Podestria under Medici and Lorraine. The center is spread on a terrace of Riolithic rock towards the ancient "carceri" with a stretch of east wall; the only door left, very restored, is the Madonnino Gate, between Vicolo Basso and Piazzetta dell'Incroccia. At the entrance from Piazza Gramsci a trachite sculpture by Renaux François.
1v73abj.42: The village on the cliff overlooking the Amiata.
fuy0k6.296: Cited from 1276, with an inscription of 1283; in the seventeenth century had the Latin cross plan, in 1822 the medieval apse was demolished and in 1953 covered the façade. Inside, frescoes from the middle of the sixteenth century attributed to Giovanni Maria di ser Giovanni Toulouse and a baptismal font from the sixteenth century.
11ra7wr.40: The 16th century frescoes of the village.
anv2hn.319: Built in 1870 by engineer Timoleone Crocchi, inspired by the Pergola of Florence, and inaugurated on August 6, 1872. In 1925 a cyclone destroyed its roof; after the war it was cinema and dance hall, closed in the seventies and reopened in 1985, after the restoration, with ÂPensaci, Giacomino! by Pirandello.
18mig53.390: In the eleventh century of the Aldobrandeschi and stop on the salt routes, it is among the greatest examples of Gothic architecture of the northern Maremma: the mast keeps original doors and windows and the rectangular tower to the south has two large rooms with vaults. The village, built around the citadel, has alleys carved into the rock and an ancient cistern that supplied the whole community.
v0ai5q.51: The Gothic fortress overlooking the Maremma plain.
1sipb4.455: Probably the Fortress Norsina already known around 952, takes its name from the sons of Tederigo, vassals of the Aldobrandeschi (1239); it passed to Siena, to the Salimbeni in 1369 and in 1618 was a fief of the Malaspina. The village is camouflaged between large boulders of riolite, 'i bossi', with arched door, alleys, arches and stairs; the remains of the casero near the Clock Tower, the wash-houses of the early twentieth century and, outside the center, the liberty Villa del Paradiso.
16wiwjd.34: The village nestled among the rocks.
10d8f9s.381: On a rocky spur at the southern end of the village, with a single nave with a flat apse and wooden roof; a 1489 plaque on the façade recalls great works, other extensions at the end of the eighteenth century. Inside a baptismal font in marble of the fifteenth century and a sixteenth-century table of Sienese school with the Madonna and Child and Saint Augustine who holds the castle of Roccatederighi.
1v8xdmn.39: The table with the picture of the castle.
10r2uqf.356: Gate of the National Park of the Metalliferous Hills on the lignite route: of the mine of Ribolla you visit most of the original complex, with accommodation and dormitories, recreation room, lighthouses and wells. Here in 1954 a gas leak killed 43 miners, one of the most serious mining tragedies of the post-war period: the site is also a place of memory today.
1knoomp.44: The history of the mine and its miners.
1lq6mqz.368: Established in 1996 between Roccastrada and Monticiano, on the border between the provinces of Siena and Grosseto: in the valley bottom beech, maples, birch and badgers, on the slopes north chestnuts and cork; live marten, skunk, wild cat and two species of bats. Along the Ferriere path you will find the Ferriera Mill, in the middle of the thirteenth century and well preserved.
1wqg9zc.59: Woods and clear waters in the heart of the Metalliferous Hills.
1wukw60.202: Ruins of the monastery in the valley of the river Bai, on a spur of trachyte halfway between Roccastrada and Montemassi; there remains also the crypt, which the municipality defines as a small treasure of the territory.
m073eo.50: A lost monastery between Roccastrada and Montemassi.
11z4c4w.332: Remains of the lock on the Bruna river wanted by the Republic of Siena in 1462, designed in 1468 and finished in 1481 for the fish culture, considered the oldest brick closed entirely on a river; a flood destroyed it eleven years later. It is partly located in Roccastrada (123 m on the left bank) and partly in Gavorrano.
1jy441q.353: In the oak, oak and chestnut woods around the village: the Fonte della Lama, in stone, cited in Leopoldini documents and for a long time a public wash-house; The Fonte di via della Fonte, with arch and seventeenth-century tub in trachyte already from the Abbey of Giugnano; the Fonte dell'amore e della passione, in trachyte, made by the artists of the Stone Road.
rpvhdj.38: A tour of springs and stone washbasins.
1p81ado.311: Medieval village on the inner hills of the Maremma, the land of Morellino di Scansano DOCG; in the surroundings the Etruscan settlement of Ice Forte, in the village the Pretorio Palace with the Archaeological Museum and the Museum of Life and Wine, the Collegiate Church of San Giovanni Battista and, on the hill, the Convent of Petreto.
fc75up.394: Etruscan village founded in the fourth century BC near the border of Vulci, on the right of the Albegna, perhaps refuge from the Roman assaults or center of wine producers; it was conquered and devastated in 280 BC. The best preserved part is the 1 km long walls and about 4 meters thick; inside the remains of the small Temple of a farm deity, whose ex-vote are at the Archaeological Museum.
1ubh1bp.44: The most powerful Etruscan walls of the Maremma.
99x62e.373: In the Palazzo Pretorio of the fifteenth century, restored in 1998, it tells of the human presence in the Valle dell'Albegna from prehistory to the Etruscans and the Romans. It exhibits the Hellenistic finds of Ice Strong (ceramics, bronze statuettes, objects related to fertility rites) and reconstructions of the Roman villa at the farm Aia Nova, with parts of the floors in cottage.
aamgnp.277: In the same Palazzo Pretorio, in five sections, it tells the link between climate, soil and wine, with objects and recipes in dialect, and presents the six DOCs of the territory, including Bianco di Pitigliano and Ansonica. Morellino di Scansano has been DOC since 1978 and DOCG since the 2006 harvest.
1vfz1og.345: Borgo probably arose in the thirteenth century, with a castle of the Aldobrandeschi then became a monastery; from the sixteenth century it passed to the counts of Santa Fiora, which drew its current layout. Under the Lorraine, the public offices of Grosseto moved there in the summer (the extant). It preserves numerous medieval buildings and views of the countryside.
6fz49o.38: The hamlet of the extaturation is grossetana.
fsk2hj.63: Church of medieval origin transformed into collegiate in 1630.
tyvk3m.31: The main church of the village.
1sxzp9t.157: On the hill that dominates the village, among oak woods, holm oaks, cypresses and pine trees, it preserves traces of the Aldobrandesque walls and a church with Romanesque foundations.
8x8kc0.40: The convent in the woods above the village.
hr2fz8.290: The Morellino di Scansano DOCG, made from Sangiovese grapes, is one of the most famous red wines in Tuscany; wineries in the village and surroundings offer tastings, and Scansano is a stop of one of the wine roads of the Maremma. At the end of September the Grape Festival closes a month of tastings and open wineries.
o2s92h.34: Tasting the Morellino where it is born.
